metric: Businesses identifying a breach or attack
comparable_note: Counts ORGANISATIONS affected, not attacks. Not comparable with an incident count.
method: Representative survey of UK businesses by Ipsos; 43% identified a breach or attack, scaled to the UK business population. Official statistics under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
notes: Headline figure. Down from 50% in the previous edition.

metric: Estimated cyber crimes committed against UK businesses
comparable_note: The closest published figure to an ATTACK count. One country, one year.
method: Survey-derived estimate scaled to the UK business population.
notes: Figure seen in secondary coverage of the release; confirm against the GOV.UK tables before quoting.

metric: Businesses that were victims of cyber crime specifically
comparable_note: A narrower measure than 'breach or attack': excludes attempts repelled without harm.
notes: Confirm against the GOV.UK tables before quoting.

metric: Businesses identifying a breach or attack
comparable_note: Same measure as the 2025/2026 row; shown to give the year-on-year movement.
method: Representative survey; 50% of businesses identified a breach or attack.
notes: Previous edition. The fall to 43% is itself contested as measurement rather than improvement.

source: Crime in England and Wales: year ending December 2025
metric: Computer misuse incidents experienced by adults
comparable_note: Individuals, not organisations. Cannot be added to business figures.
method: Crime Survey for England and Wales: face-to-face victimisation survey of adults aged 16+, scaled to the population. The canonical 'dark figure' method.
notes: No statistically significant change on the previous year.

source: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2025
metric: Computer misuse incidents experienced by adults
method: Crime Survey for England and Wales, scaled to the population.
notes: A 32% decrease on the previous year, driven by a fall in unauthorised access to personal information.

source: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2017
metric: Computer misuse incidents experienced by adults
comparable_note: Earliest comparable year. Shows the survey measure has FALLEN by 61% while recorded incidents here have risen.
method: Crime Survey for England and Wales, first year computer misuse was included.
notes: The divergence between this series and the recorded series is the single most useful thing on this page.

source: Crime in England and Wales: year ending March 2025
comparable_note: Fraud, much of it cyber-enabled, is counted separately from computer misuse. Not all of this is a cyber attack.
method: Crime Survey for England and Wales, scaled to the population.
notes: Highest since fraud was first collected in 2017. Included for scale, with the caveat that definitions differ.
